title: Victorian privacy regulator finds Education Department breached privacy law after school-system breach
date_note: IDM published on 20 November 2026; the breach was notified to OVIC on 7 January 2026.
summary: IDM reports that the Office of the Victorian Information Commissioner (OVIC) found the Department of Education contravened Information Privacy Principles 4.1 and 4.2. An attacker compromised one government school's IT system and reached a database covering every government school student, including names, school email addresses and encrypted passwords. OVIC made seven recommendations due by 31 December 2026; the department accepted all seven.
plain: Victoria's privacy regulator found the state education department kept former students' login data and did not protect it adequately before a breach.
exec: Keeping credentials of past users and incomplete vulnerability remediation can breach privacy law.
action: Review policies for retaining past users' credentials, and confirm that critical vulnerability advisories are acted on across all sites.
impact: Former students affected: hundreds of thousands, per IDM.

validation.note: Single publisher (IDM) reporting OVIC's findings; the OVIC report PDF was not read.

review.note: Compared with IDM: IPP 4.1/4.2, one school's system, all-student database, data types, seven recommendations due 31 Dec 2026 accepted, 7 Jan 2026 notification, hundreds of thousands former students
